# llms.txt — guide for AI assistants working on this repository

## What this is

multica-setup bootstraps a project team in [Multica](https://multica.ai):
a squad of agent teammates, a kanban flow with explicit handoffs, and
recurring automations. The entire tool is **one Python file**
(`bin/multica-setup`, standard library only, Python 3.10+) that drives
Multica exclusively through the `multica` CLI — it never calls any API
directly.

## Repository map

| Path | What it is |
|---|---|
| `bin/multica-setup` | The CLI (~2500 lines). Bare run = interactive menu; subcommands `init / check / plan / apply / status / smoke / teardown` |
| `templates/project.example.json` | A complete runnable manifest |
| `templates/project.schema.md` | Field reference for manifests — keep it in sync with the code |
| `roles/<role>.md` | Per-role agent instructions, rendered into each agent |
| `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` | Shared skills (frontmatter `name:` + `description:`, then markdown) |
| `squad/squad-instructions.md` | Squad routing/handoff/sign-off instructions |
| `autopilots/<key>.md` | Runbooks rendered into autopilot descriptions |
| `docs/runbook.md` | Operations + troubleshooting — keep current with behavior changes |
| `docs/how-it-works.md`, `docs/flow.md` | Design and the kanban/handoff contract |
| `README.md` | User-facing; "Good to know" must reflect real behavior |

## How the pieces connect

manifest (JSON spec) → `Manifest` dataclass → `build_context()` →
`render()` → `Multica` client (subprocess calls to `multica ...
--workspace-id ... --output json`) → `Plan` (dry = plan, else apply) →
steps in order: workspace → skills → agents → squad → project →
autopilots.

- `render()` substitutes `{{placeholder}}` strictly: a placeholder missing
  from the context, or one left unrendered, raises `ManifestError`. The
  context keys are exactly: `project_name`, `project_description`,
  `repo_list`, `squad_name`, `issue_prefix`, `roster`, `routing_table`,
  `routing_bullets`, and `<role>_name` for every role.
- The spec lives in a local `<workspace>.json` file or inside Multica
  (in `--in-project` mode it is stored in the managed project's
  description as an HTML comment block and read back via
  `multica project list`).
- `plan` is a dry `apply`; both diff spec vs live CLI state, so re-runs
  are no-ops when nothing drifted.

## Editing rules for AI

`bin/multica-setup`:
- No dependencies, no type hints, no comments except
  `# ---- section ----` banners. Match the existing style; keep
  functions small.
- After ANY edit run:
  `python3 -c "import ast; ast.parse(open('bin/multica-setup').read())"`
- The `Multica` client methods wrap CLI calls and `unwrap_list()` JSON
  envelopes; `MulticaError` wraps non-zero exits with the CLI's stderr.

Add a **role**: `ROLES` + `ROLE_BLURBS` (top of the file) +
`roles/<key>.md` + entries in `ROUTE_TABLE`/`ROUTE_BULLETS` and the
`attach_to` lists in `cmd_init`'s `skills` + a line in
`templates/project.schema.md` and the README. `lead` is the only
required role — new roles must be optional.

Add an **autopilot runbook**: `autopilots/<key>.md` in the house voice
(address the project owner; `## Steps` numbered; `## Boundaries`
explicit; output is ONE comment on the autopilot's own issue; on broken
tooling post the failure and stop, never retry-loop) + a line in
`templates/project.schema.md` + the repo map in README + the table in
`docs/runbook.md`. Defaults live in `cmd_init` (`default_ap`; git-only
runbooks in `GIT_AP_DEFS`, enabled only when repos are registered).

Add a **skill**: `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (frontmatter `name:` +
`description:`) + the manifest's `skills` list (`source: local` or `url`,
`attach_to: all` or a role list).

Calibrated CLI quirks the code depends on (multica 0.4.x — re-verify
after CLI upgrades):
- `autopilot list --output json` = `{"autopilots": [...]}`; entries carry
  `title`, not `name`
- `autopilot get` = `{"autopilot": {...}, "collaborators": [...],
  "triggers": [...]}` (schedule trigger under `triggers`)
- `issue list --output json` = `{"issues": [...], "total": ...}`
- project resources store the URL under `resource_ref.url`
- agents carry `archived_at`; teardown archives (the CLI cannot delete),
  re-apply restores via `agent restore <id>` — never re-create archived
  names
- workspace slugs on Multica Cloud are globally unique across all users

## Verification before committing

1. Parse check (above).
2. `--manifest <file> plan` on a throwaway manifest (dry, no side effects).
3. For behavior changes: full E2E on a **scratch** workspace —
   `bin/multica-setup init --auto --new-workspace "<name>" --slug
   <random> --project "<name>" --runtime opencode` → verify via the
   `multica` CLI → `--workspace <slug> ... teardown --yes` → ask the user
   to delete the workspace shell in the web UI.
4. NEVER run `apply`/`teardown` against a production workspace
   (e.g. the user's real projects) without explicit instruction.

## Repository conventions

- Commit identity via environment variables only (never touch git
  config): `GIT_AUTHOR_NAME="Peter Frank" GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL="info@peterfrank.se"`
  and the same for `GIT_COMMITTER_*`.
- Tag a release per coherent feature batch: `git tag -a <version> -m
  "multica-setup <version>: <summary>"`, push `origin main <tag>`.
- Never commit user files that appear in the working tree; stage exactly
  the files you changed.
- Keep `README.md` ("Good to know", repo map), `docs/runbook.md`, and
  `templates/project.schema.md` consistent with any behavior change.
